title: ward status names a format version that is no longer the vault document's
description: WCLI-11 moved the vault state document to format 2 (DEC-19 B). The sealed envelope has its own version and stayed 1, and ward status prints the envelope one, which ADR 0007 records as deliberate because it is readable without the key. Before WCLI-11 both numbers were 1, so the line read correctly; now a healthy vault reports "format version 1" in the same release whose refusal says a vault from another version cannot be read. Measured at e765951: ward status prints "present (revision N, format version 1)" for a vault this build reads happily, and ward doctor schema check reports pass/current on the same vault. Whether the fix is the wording or the reported number is a design question for opum-agent, because changing the printed text is a user-facing string under DEC-10 and changing the number means status has to parse the state, which ADR 0007 deliberately avoids so status answers without the key.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The printed line and the JSON field can no longer be mistaken for the state document format when they are the envelope format, and whichever way that is achieved is recorded where ADR 0007 states the existing claim.
A test pins the answer against a vault this build writes, so a future bump that moves one version without the other is a red build rather than a review miss.

implementationNotes: EXTENDED after the WCLI-11 independent review (F1), which measured a second, sharper half of this. ward status does not merely print the envelope version where a reader might expect the state document one: on a vault whose state document is format 1 and whose envelope is unchanged, ward status --json exits 0 with vault.status present and binding.status unknown, and the word unsupported appears nowhere in the report. ward doctor does report it, as state_unsupported on its schema check. That is by design under ADR 0007, which has status answer from the sealed header alone so it works without the key, so status genuinely cannot know. The defect is therefore in ADR 0010, which claimed status reported the unsupported state; the ADR is corrected where the branch files this. What remains for this task is not a bug fix but a decision, and it has the same shape as the version-number half: whether ward status should say something about a state document it cannot read, and if so whether that means loading the key and giving up the answer-without-the-key property ADR 0007 chose. Measured at 90024fe; the reviewer reached it independently of the version-number finding.
